title: The symmetric Mahler conjecture and its equality cases
scope_note: Pinned authored main source and all eight included body sections read completely. Figure captions read in source; rendered figure PDFs, bibliography entries, third-party TeX implementation packages and separate Lean formalizations are outside this full-body reading scope. sections_read: Introduction, including historical context and both functional and entropy–transport corollaries
Polarity, norm sums, Hanner recursion and volume products
Conformal lens, boundary law and endpoint scaling
Isolated holomorphic-zero mass, Stokes normalization and Cauchy–Binet
Boundary feasibility and probability-zero extra boundary ties
Real feasible-simplex identity and arbitrary-body approximation
Zero-deficit common witness including degenerate limiting representations
Endpoint costs, metric medians, three balls and equality classification
claim_as_stated: For every origin-symmetric convex body K in R^n, |K||K°|≥4^n/n!, with equality exactly for invertible linear images of Hanner polytopes. The introduction also derives the even functional Mahler and symmetric entropy–transport inequalities from the claimed all-dimensional geometric result.
proof_architecture: Construct a convex conformal lens whose uniform boundary angle gives an independent uniform sign and a uniform imaginary coordinate; establish strict curvature and λ(1−η)∼(2/π)η log(1/η).

Use Stokes around an isolated homogeneous holomorphic zero to lower-bound total squared Jacobian-minor mass, then apply it to high powers of inverse-lens coordinate maps. Rescaled radial variables yield Σ_I P_I≥1 over independent row bases.

Convert each boundary feasibility probability into a real integral with factor |det B_I|/4^d. Extra ties are null, and unique maximizers make feasible signed simplices disjoint in interior, giving 1≤d!4^(−d)∫|Σ_X|≤d!4^(−d)|A||A°|. Approximate arbitrary symmetric bodies.

For equality lift by one segment, approximate the polar product by inner polytopes, and turn vanishing integrated missing volume into nearby feasible point–direction pairs using positive-volume product neighborhoods. Compactness gives one common feasibility witness even for degenerate limiting row representations.

Compare all positive representations using that common witness. Let the point approach the lifted apex; the endpoint ratio of λ yields support inequalities and a median for each triple in the polar norm.

Convert medians to the three-ball intersection property and invoke Hansen–Lima's finite-dimensional classification. Polarity and norm-sum formulas identify precisely the linear Hanner equality bodies.

construction_ideas.idea: A global minor-mass budget can locate a nonzero feasible basis before optimizing its cost.
assumptions: The candidate row family spans the intended determinant dimension, over the field relevant to the integer determinant.
A holomorphic constraint construction can be made whose minor factors are the same candidate determinants and whose compact sublevels and isolated zero are proved.
An additional cost-weighted estimate, absent from the manuscript's ΣP_I≥1 statement, controls the total degree/height of a feasible basis.
construction_ideas.speculative_interface: For candidate row transversals Q(Z), attach strip constraints to the actual row vectors and view Σ_I P_I as a distribution of independent bases. Test a cost filtration by column degree/denominator size and seek a mass inequality concentrated below the analytic smallness threshold. This could separate proving some minor nonzero from charging its columns, but the existing lemma alone gives no cheap basis and cannot repair deficient rank.

construction_ideas.idea: A single dual feasibility witness can certify all competing row costs, including singular limits.
assumptions: The proposed determinant/column costs admit a convex positive-representation or matroid base formulation.
The same chosen witness is valid for every candidate constraint; competitors cannot each choose a different witness.
Any zero-deficit-to-pointwise upgrade uses positive-volume neighborhoods and actual compactness, rather than assuming pointwise convergence.
construction_ideas.speculative_interface: Represent a target signature or budget direction by costed candidate rows. Find a dual vector Y giving c_i·Y=cost_i on selected rows and h·Y≤cost_h on every candidate. Then every competing representation has cost at least ξ·Y. The manuscript's integrated deficit and degenerate-limit treatment suggest how to retain such a certificate when candidate bases coalesce. Apply first to a finite model of signature capacities/Q(Z), keeping this optimization certificate separate from the needed integer nonzero determinant.

limits: No independent checking of the claimed Mahler resolution or its external classification inputs was performed.
ΣP_I≥1 concerns an already spanning finite row family; it does not prove rank for the user's actual determinant.
The lens includes π in its normalization, so reusing the analytic device in a π rational-approximation argument requires a noncircular definition and explicit integrality/denominator accounting.
No degree/height estimate suitable for BA or non-BA π is supplied by this geometric proof.

scope_note: Pinned authored main source, all eight included body sections, complete finite-consequences appendix and all three included figure sources read completely. sections_read: Introduction and conventions
Entire latent alphabet gadget and latent-recursion figure
Outer weighted parity questions, clone preprocessing, exact table keys, folding and completeness
Entire inverse-shortcode derivation, spectral comparison, good-row-fiber extraction, padded-law comparison, witness transfer, Fourier decoding and advice figure
Entire clean-coordinate soundness argument and fixed matrix-game gap
Entire rounding/subdivision, parameter selection and explicit encoding completion
All approximation consequences: Max-Cut, Vertex Cover, CSP, ordering, cut/deletion/clustering and companion qualifications

All included body and appendix proof text; no body section excluded by relevance
claim_as_stated: For each fixed ε,δ∈(0,1/2), a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to explicit unweighted simple bipartite Unique Games over a fixed K=F_2^s has completeness≥1−ε and soundness≤δ; every edge is a translation constraint. This is a manuscript claim, not independently validated.
proof_architecture: Construct latent additive noise using characteristic-two quadratic finite-field blocks. Uniform genericity over every linear extension map and random orientations permit adaptive restrictions; the harmonic potential H_r retains positive rank while nonlinear change decays. Quotient shift kernels and add injection-indexed copies to realize any sufficiently large fixed output alphabet.

Preprocess a weighted nearly satisfiable parity gap to three distinct variable IDs per occurrence. Form affine table keys that retain support, actual-bit coordinates and exact intercepts; identify keys through projection and fold free constant translations. The resulting rank-one equality test has near completeness from global assignment evaluation.

Fourier comparison turns high latent-test acceptance into ordinary shortcode acceptance. Grassmann expansion yields a bounded row/column slice. Erase all good row fibers and apply concentration uniformly over every slice–target description to force positive good-advice mass; folding forces a nonempty short set of actual answers.

Compare the full sparse-projection padded table law with unrestricted sampling by a product chi-squared bound: kβ²→0. Transfer the selected witness using a positive probability difference, then a private Fourier decoder reaches the projected short answer set with fixed positive probability. The decoder never receives the other side’s witness.

Choose β=k^(−2/3), so kβ→∞ clean singleton coordinates remain. Condition only on the clean mask, advice intercept and outside data, retaining the independent equation–variable law. Each side reconstructs its original local input; projection-game repetition makes full agreement at most exp(−c k^(1/3)), contradicting the decoded constant lower bound.

Largest-remainder rounding, four-edge subdivision and alphabet-independent repetition give explicit unweighted simple bipartite translation games with prescribed errors. Check quantifier order and polynomial encoding. The appendix supplies simple strong-left games and a rational finite ordering composition using local smoothing, low-influence estimates, influence decoding and conditioning on distinct neighbors.

construction_ideas.idea: Use a harmonic rank potential to compare useful contraction against loss of independence.
assumptions: A concrete family of permitted row/column restrictions has rank drop at most one per step, with conditional loss probability≤c r θ at current rank r.
The rank-loss estimate holds for every extension map that earlier choices can induce; assuming independence from an adaptive construction is insufficient.
The operation improves the analytic determinant size on the same object and preserves its integer structure.
construction_ideas.speculative_interface: In a costed-column determinant construction, track H_r=Σ_{j≤r}1/j instead of raw remaining rank. If collisions among candidate Q(Z) row transversals have probability O(rθ), expected H_r loss is O(θ), permitting many smallness-improving steps while retaining positive rank with explicit probability. A finite simulation should measure rank loss conditioned on signature occupancy, then test whether candidate selection obeys a uniform extension-map bound.

construction_ideas.idea: Prove genericity uniformly over adversarial coefficients using an augmented nonzero minor.
assumptions: The evaluation vectors have algebraic parameter dependence and an algebraic obstruction to column-span membership.
A nonzero polynomial minor is established symbolically before specializing parameters.
Finite-field genericity must be replaced or lifted with explicit integer heights and rational-approximation errors for the actual π problem.
construction_ideas.speculative_interface: The latent proof handles all maps g simultaneously by showing a nonlinear target evaluation vector is outside a matrix column span, then exhibits one augmented minor as a nonzero bounded-degree polynomial. For quadratic occupancy/signature constraints, formulate potential zero terms as target-in-span conditions; prove a formal augmented minor nonzero via monomial/parity support, then specialize integer parameters away from its zero set while costing the specialization. This is a route to certify that structural zero terms do not consume every candidate, rather than counting signatures alone.

construction_ideas.idea: Keep nonlinear stability and linear detection as separately quantified requirements.
assumptions: The two properties are verified under the exact same noise or perturbation law.
Nonlinear error probability and linear detection threshold are fixed before ambient dimension/number of columns grows.
Any lifting to rational approximation controls denominator growth from products and quotients.
construction_ideas.speculative_interface: Treat the analytic smallness of an integral or Padé-type column as the stable nonlinear observable, and determinant rank as detection by a linear family. Search for a perturbation of row choices that changes analytic errors rarely but is detected by any large annihilator/signature space. The manuscript shows that these goals can coexist abstractly; it does not construct such a perturbation for π.

construction_ideas.idea: Use a sparse perturbation regime with many useful coordinates but asymptotically unchanged full law.
assumptions: Independent block contributions have a bounded chi-squared divergence between the ordinary and special-coordinate laws.
The ambient alphabet and all local dimensions are fixed before the number k of blocks grows.
A nonzero determinant or capacity event is transferred using the joint table distribution; agreement of separate marginals is insufficient.
construction_ideas.speculative_interface: For candidate row transversals Q(Z), design a mixture that marks a coordinate with probability β. A full-law bound of order kβ² can vanish while kβ diverges, giving many special rows under nearly the same candidate distribution. β=k^(−2/3) balances these requirements. This is directly relevant to quadratic occupancy: a proposed capacity improvement should be checked under the actual joint row law and include the cost of conditioning on distinct/signature-safe selections. It remains speculative until the local likelihood ratio and determinant nonvanishing event are established.

limits: No independent verification of the claimed Unique Games resolution or of the exact cited external expansion/repetition/invariance hypotheses was performed.
The finite-field genericity, characteristic-two trace and square-root calculations do not automatically transfer to characteristic zero.
The enormous but finite recursive gadget and all constants are fixed before input size; the proof supplies no usable integer-height or denominator bounds for rational approximation.
A distributional or combinatorial analogy supplies neither an integer determinant nonzero certificate nor an analytic estimate below one for that same determinant.
No theorem about π, irrationality measure, BA or non-BA follows.

title: Uniform bounds for planar polynomial limit cycles

Primitive proofs in07–08 are read but their earlier abstract packet/calculus hypotheses await the other reading.
sections_read: Introduction: uniform boundedness statement, historical context, proof strategy and analytic interfaces

Finite logarithmic flags in full: saturation preserving free coordinates, bounded-background stability, paths through anchors, real/angular path estimates, nested contours, background jet sensitivity, exceptional anchor constants, common safe columns
Macros and proof-roadmap figure source

Entire section 07: one-rate regular/stable passages, actual continuation, formal normalization and tails, Gevrey optimal truncation, finite charge expansion, ordered dispersal, controlled derivatives and retestability

Entire section 08: comparable/small/fast two-scale regimes, integration trees, colliding-cost residue clusters, meromorphic coefficients and safe columns, compatible input/output charts, full-chart Gevrey estimates, cutoff retirement, support/germ invariance and primitive-library uniformity

Entire section 09: exact subanalytic preparation, Euler-center change and contact bins, complete pole/balance radius list, pole-free box compact jet estimates, finite box induction with 2m+e potential, one resonant redo, boundary Jordan crossings and finite passage words
claim_as_stated: For every degree d≥1 there is a finite B(d) bounding the number of limit cycles of every real planar polynomial vector field of degree≤d throughout the plane, without coefficient/stability restrictions; no effective formula for B(d) is claimed.
proof_architecture: Encode an alleged escaping solution sequence in a finite saturated logarithmic flag Z_1≫…≫Z_m≫1 with exact triangular log relations; preserve existing free coordinates when promoting vanishing ordinary coordinates.

Construct complex paths through far anchors independent of ordinary backgrounds. Quantitative angular rates produce nested good contours and buffered sides where a selected exponential scale dominates later ones; finite-jet controls retain these margins under changes of background.

The introduction states that two lateral asymptotic packet trees, with full domain/transition/error data, yield a first nonzero term or exact vanishing via weighted Cauchy corrections and maximum principles. Differentiated implicit calculus and elimination would then contradict isolated escaping zeros.

The full one-rate section 07 and mixed-clock section 08 construct actual holomorphic passage maps and finite-charge descriptions. They use formal normalization, fixed-one-side tail convergence, Gevrey optimal truncation, exact clusters at colliding residue costs, safe meromorphic columns, compatible endpoint charts and ordered retirement of numerical cutoffs. Earlier abstract packet/calculus hypotheses and the additive section06 remain unread by this reader.

The fully read geometric section 09 uses simultaneous subanalytic preparation of rational fields, including every pole modulus and numerator balance radius. Compact pole-free rational families have finite jet-order bounds; the induction potential 2m+e terminates box refinements, and a one-redo argument controls nonzero resonances. Jordan-curve crossing signs bound boundary events, yielding a finite passage alphabet and bounded cyclic words uniformly over coefficient degeneracies.

An independent absolute-to-uniform projection-counting principle is stated to bound fiber components, hence hyperbolic cycles. Signed rotation and spatial rescaling are stated to include nonhyperbolic isolated cycles throughout the plane.

construction_ideas.idea: Protect zero-term analysis by an exact scale flag and distinguish zero germs from cancellation on a sequence.
assumptions: Every determinant contribution/error term can be expressed in a finite ordered collection of actual scales, with exact dependencies and bounded ordinary backgrounds.
After cancellation, an asserted leading coefficient is a nonzero analytic germ, not merely nonzero at selected sample points.
Any claim that all asymptotic terms vanishing implies exact zero requires a proved domain/separation theorem; real flatness alone is inadequate.
construction_ideas.speculative_interface: For Δ_N(q,p) built from costed columns near p/q≈π, encode factorial, exponential and powers of q scales in a flag and reduce exact dependencies before ordering determinant terms. Label the zero-term loss by the first genuinely nonzero signature coefficient. Preserve free approximation scale variables when inserting −log|qπ−p|. This could expose where quadratic occupancy arguments count only formally distinct terms that actually cancel.

construction_ideas.idea: Use finite-request safe intervals to avoid all finitely many bad denominator or pole lattices without asserting equidistribution.
assumptions: Relevant sweeps are eventually increasing with derivatives tending to infinity and |x''/(x')²|≤C/x.
Only a fixed finite list of bad lattices is excluded at a given determinant size.
The application needs continuous parameter choices or a separate integer-point argument; safe real columns do not automatically supply integer N/q.
construction_ideas.speculative_interface: When coefficient transformations create finitely many sine, gamma or reciprocal factors, select a common detuned parameter interval by bounding time spent near each bad lattice and union bounding; no independence or incommensurability of sweeps is needed. Then separately prove an allowed integer index exists in that interval and charge the interval width. This could stabilize candidate-row transversals near singular factors but is not itself a Diophantine approximation theorem.

construction_ideas.idea: Maintain explicit buffers and fixed derivative-loss exponents before strengthening accuracy.
assumptions: The analytic upper bound can be continued to complex domains with quantitative buffers, not just real estimates.
Only finitely many derivative/coherence orders are needed per determinant and all cost exponents are fixed before accuracy is increased.
Dependent scales are reevaluated at current background values after implicit changes.
construction_ideas.speculative_interface: For a near-vanishing determinant perturbation or parameter correction, write a ledger of analytic decay versus derivative and denominator losses. Reserve a positive buffer that survives the row/column transformations. The flags proof's hierarchy and high finite-jet sensitivity suggest a disciplined way to prevent a later approximation accuracy requirement from silently increasing the column-degree budget past the small-integer threshold.

construction_ideas.idea: Combine colliding terms exactly before separating costs or taking absolute values.
assumptions: A finite cluster identity is proved at coinciding exponents or signatures, with its removable singularities retained.
Every clustered coefficient is added using exact algebra before calling it nonzero or estimating its size.
The same clustered object remains an integer after denominator clearing; this must be checked separately.
construction_ideas.speculative_interface: The mixed-passage proof keeps the analytic residue cluster (exp(−C0 L)−exp(−C1 L))/(C1−C0), whose equal-cost limit is L exp(−C0 L), instead of treating two singular residue terms separately. In the determinant expansion for π, group row transversals with the same signature/exponent before capacity counting. A signature may have many combinatorial occupants but a zero total coefficient. Conversely near collisions may contribute polynomial prefactors rather than independent exponential terms. Derive an exact cluster formula first, then cost its polynomial factor in the analytic smallness ledger.
